```{r data}
# ---- Data ----
A <- as.matrix(read.table("data/A.txt"))
dimnames(A) <- NULL
d00 <- scan("data/seis00.txt", quiet = TRUE)
d01 <- scan("data/seis01.txt", quiet = TRUE)
d02 <- scan("data/seis02.txt", quiet = TRUE)
n <- nrow(A)
idx <- 1:n
```

```{r functions}
# ---- Helper functions ----

# exponential covariance, S_ij = s2 * exp(-3|i-j|/l)
cov_exp <- function(n, s2, l) {
  s2 * exp(-3 * abs(outer(1:n, 1:n, "-")) / l)
}

# posterior of m given d (Gaussian conditioning, 1a)
post_m <- function(d, mu, S, s2e) {
  S_d <- A %*% S %*% t(A) + s2e * diag(n)
  K <- S %*% t(A) %*% solve(S_d)
  S_post <- S - K %*% A %*% S
  list(mean = drop(mu + K %*% (d - A %*% mu)),
       cov = (S_post + t(S_post)) / 2)
}

# k draws from N(mu, S), one per row
draw_mvn <- function(k, mu, S) {
  L <- t(chol(S + 1e-10 * diag(length(mu))))
  Z <- matrix(rnorm(length(mu) * k), length(mu), k)
  t(mu + L %*% Z)
}

# mean with 95% band, optionally some realisations on top
plot_band <- function(mean, sd, title, ylim, sims = NULL) {
  plot(idx, mean, type = "n", ylim = ylim, xlab = "i", ylab = "m", main = title)
  polygon(c(idx, rev(idx)), c(mean - 1.96 * sd, rev(mean + 1.96 * sd)),
          col = "grey85", border = NA)
  if (!is.null(sims)) matlines(idx, t(sims), lty = 1, col = 2:6)
  lines(idx, mean, lwd = 2)
}
```

# Part 1

## 1a)

$\vm$ and $\varepsilon$ are independent and Gaussian, and $\vd$ is linear in them, so
$(\vm,\vd)$ is jointly Gaussian with
\begin{align*}
E(\vd) &= \vA\mu_m,\\
\operatorname{Cov}(\vd) &= \vA\Sigma_m\vA^\top+\sigma_\varepsilon^2\vI \;=:\; \Sigma_d,\\
\operatorname{Cov}(\vd,\vm) &= \operatorname{Cov}(\vA\vm+\varepsilon,\vm)=\vA\Sigma_m,
\end{align*}
so
$$
\begin{pmatrix}\vm\\ \vd\end{pmatrix}\sim N\!\left(
\begin{pmatrix}\mu_m\\ \vA\mu_m\end{pmatrix},
\begin{pmatrix}\Sigma_m & \Sigma_m\vA^\top\\
\vA\Sigma_m & \Sigma_d\end{pmatrix}\right).
$$
Conditioning on $\vd$ gives $\vm\mid\vd\sim N(\mu_{m\mid d},\Sigma_{m\mid d})$ with
\begin{align*}
\mu_{m\mid d} &= \mu_m+\Sigma_m\vA^\top\Sigma_d^{-1}(\vd-\vA\mu_m),\\
\Sigma_{m\mid d} &= \Sigma_m-\Sigma_m\vA^\top\Sigma_d^{-1}\vA\Sigma_m .
\end{align*}

## 1b)

```{r prior, fig.cap="Prior expectation (black), 95\\% credibility interval (grey) and five simulated profiles."}
# ---- 1b ----
mu0 <- 0; s2m <- 1; l <- 20; s2e <- 0.04
mu_prior <- rep(mu0, n)
S_prior <- cov_exp(n, s2m, l)

set.seed(1)
prior_draws <- draw_mvn(5, mu_prior, S_prior)
plot_band(mu_prior, sqrt(diag(S_prior)), "Prior", c(-3.5, 3.5), prior_draws)
```

## 1c)

```{r post00, fig.cap="Posterior expectation (black) and 95\\% credibility interval (grey) for seis00. Dashed: prior interval."}
# ---- 1c ----
post00 <- post_m(d00, mu_prior, S_prior, s2e)
plot_band(post00$mean, sqrt(diag(post00$cov)), "Posterior, seis00", c(-3.5, 3.5))
abline(h = c(-1.96, 1.96), lty = 2, col = "grey40")
```

```{r covimages, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=3.6, fig.cap="Prior (left) and posterior (right) covariance matrices, same colour scale."}
plot_cov <- function(S, title, zlim) {
  image(idx, idx, t(S)[, n:1], zlim = zlim, col = hcl.colors(64, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE),
        xlab = "j", ylab = "i", main = title, axes = FALSE)
  axis(1)
  axis(2, at = n + 1 - c(1, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100), labels = c(1, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100))
  box()
}
zlim <- range(S_prior, post00$cov)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
plot_cov(S_prior, "Prior covariance", zlim)
plot_cov(post00$cov, "Posterior covariance", zlim)
```

## 1d)

```{r exceedance}
# ---- 1d ----
cval <- -1
volume <- function(m) sum((cval - m) * (m < cval))

B <- 100
set.seed(2)
m_draws <- draw_mvn(B, post00$mean, post00$cov)
V <- apply(m_draws, 1, volume)

V_stats <- c(mean = mean(V), median = median(V), sd = sd(V))
knitr::kable(t(round(V_stats, 2)), caption = "Posterior mean, median and sd of $V$ ($B=100$).")
```

```{r Vhist, fig.width=5.5, fig.height=3.2, fig.cap="Histogram of 100 posterior samples of $V$."}
hist(V, breaks = 20, col = "grey80", border = "white", main = "", xlab = "V")
```

## 1e)

```{r percentiles}
# ---- 1e ----
V_sorted <- sort(V)
P10 <- V_sorted[10]
P90 <- V_sorted[90]

# number below P10 is Bin(B, 0.1)
r <- qbinom(0.025, B, 0.1)
s <- qbinom(0.975, B, 0.1) + 1
cover <- pbinom(s - 1, B, 0.1) - pbinom(r - 1, B, 0.1)
```

We use the 10th and 90th smallest of the 100 samples:
$\widehat P_{10}=`r round(P10, 2)`$ and $\widehat P_{90}=`r round(P90, 2)`$.

The number of samples below $P_{10}$ is $N\sim\mathrm{Bin}(100,0.1)$, and $P_{10}$ lies
between the $r$-th and $s$-th smallest sample when $r\le N\le s-1$:
$$
P\big(V_{(r)}\le P_{10}<V_{(s)}\big)=\sum_{k=r}^{s-1}\binom{100}{k}0.1^k0.9^{100-k}.
$$
With $r=`r r`$ and $s=`r s`$ this is `r round(cover, 3)`, so a 95% interval for $P_{10}$ is
$[`r round(V_sorted[r], 2)`,\ `r round(V_sorted[s], 2)`]$. This is wide, so 100 samples is not enough.

## 1f)

```{r permtest, fig.width=5.5, fig.height=3.2, fig.cap="Lag-1 correlation for 1000 permutations of seis00 (histogram) and for the observed data (red line)."}
# ---- 1f ----
lag1 <- function(x) cor(x[-1], x[-length(x)])

rho <- lag1(d00)
set.seed(4)
rho_perm <- replicate(1000, lag1(sample(d00)))

hist(rho_perm, breaks = 30, col = "grey80", border = "white", main = "",
     xlab = "Lag-1 correlation", xlim = c(-0.4, 1))
abline(v = rho, col = "red", lwd = 2)
```

The observed lag-1 correlation is `r round(rho, 2)`, larger than all 1000 permuted
values ($p<0.001$). The data are therefore not exchangeable.

# Part 2

## 2a)

Only the prior mean depends on $(T,B)$, so from 1a
$$
p(\vd\mid T,B)=N\big(\vd;\ \vA\mu_m^{T,B},\ \Sigma_d\big),\qquad
\Sigma_d=\vA\Sigma_m\vA^\top+\sigma_\varepsilon^2\vI ,
$$
and by Bayes' rule, for $(T,B)\in\mathcal G$,
$$
p(T,B\mid\vd)=\frac{p(\vd\mid T,B)\,p(T,B)}{\sum_{(T',B')\in\mathcal G}p(\vd\mid T',B')\,p(T',B')}
\;\propto\;\exp\!\Big\{-\tfrac12(\vd-\vA\mu_m^{T,B})^\top\Sigma_d^{-1}(\vd-\vA\mu_m^{T,B})\Big\},
$$
since the uniform prior and the normalising constant do not depend on $(T,B)$.

```{r p2setup}
# ---- 2a ----
dmu <- 5
pairs <- subset(expand.grid(T = 30:60, B = 40:70), T <= B)
pairs$dZ <- pairs$B - pairs$T + 1

# prior mean with a zone from T to B (T = NA means no zone)
zone_mean <- function(T, B) {
  m <- rep(mu0, n)
  if (!is.na(T)) m[T:B] <- mu0 - dmu
  m
}

S_d <- A %*% S_prior %*% t(A) + s2e * diag(n)
L_d <- t(chol(S_d))

# log p(d | T, B) without the constant
loglik <- function(d, mu, L = L_d) {
  e <- forwardsolve(L, d - A %*% mu)
  -0.5 * sum(e^2)
}

logsumexp <- function(x) max(x) + log(sum(exp(x - max(x))))

post_TB <- function(d, L = L_d) {
  ll <- sapply(1:nrow(pairs), function(k) loglik(d, zone_mean(pairs$T[k], pairs$B[k]), L))
  list(ll = ll, prob = exp(ll - logsumexp(ll)))
}

zone01 <- post_TB(d01)
zone02 <- post_TB(d02)
```

```{r heatmaps, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=3.6, fig.cap="Joint posterior $p(T,B\\mid d)$ for seis01 (left) and seis02 (right). Grey: inadmissible pairs."}
plot_heat <- function(prob, title) {
  M <- matrix(NA, 31, 31)
  M[cbind(pairs$T - 29, pairs$B - 39)] <- prob
  image(30:60, 40:70, M, col = hcl.colors(64, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE),
        xlab = "T", ylab = "B", main = title)
  image(30:60, 40:70, ifelse(is.na(M), 1, NA), col = "grey85", add = TRUE)
  box()
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
plot_heat(zone01$prob, "seis01")
plot_heat(zone02$prob, "seis02")
```

```{r priormarg, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=2.4, fig.cap="Marginal prior of top $T$, base $B$ and thickness $\\Delta Z$ (uniform prior on $\\mathcal G$)."}
marginal <- function(w, x, vals) sapply(vals, function(v) sum(w[x == v]))
prior_TB <- rep(1 / nrow(pairs), nrow(pairs))

par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))
plot(30:60, marginal(prior_TB, pairs$T, 30:60), type = "h", lwd = 3, xlab = "T", ylab = "Prior")
plot(40:70, marginal(prior_TB, pairs$B, 40:70), type = "h", lwd = 3, xlab = "B", ylab = "Prior")
plot(1:41, marginal(prior_TB, pairs$dZ, 1:41), type = "h", lwd = 3, xlab = "dZ", ylab = "Prior")
```

```{r postmarg, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=4.4, fig.cap="Marginal posterior of $T$, $B$ and $\\Delta Z$. Top row: seis01, bottom row: seis02."}
par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))
for (z in list(zone01, zone02)) {
  plot(30:60, marginal(z$prob, pairs$T, 30:60), type = "h", lwd = 3, ylim = c(0, 1),
       xlab = "T", ylab = "Posterior")
  plot(40:70, marginal(z$prob, pairs$B, 40:70), type = "h", lwd = 3, ylim = c(0, 1),
       xlab = "B", ylab = "Posterior")
  plot(1:41, marginal(z$prob, pairs$dZ, 1:41), type = "h", lwd = 3, ylim = c(0, 1),
       xlab = "dZ", ylab = "Posterior")
}
```

```{r p2summary}
best_pair <- function(prob) {
  k <- which.max(prob)
  c(T = pairs$T[k], B = pairs$B[k], dZ = pairs$dZ[k], prob = prob[k])
}
best <- rbind(seis01 = best_pair(zone01$prob), seis02 = best_pair(zone02$prob))
```

The prior marginals are not uniform, since the number of possible partners varies.
The posterior puts almost all mass on $(41,46)$ for seis01 (probability
`r round(best[1, "prob"], 3)`) and $(41,61)$ for seis02 (probability
`r round(best[2, "prob"], 3)`), i.e. thickness `r best[1, "dZ"]` and `r best[2, "dZ"]`.
The data determine the zone almost exactly.

## 2b)

If all 752 models (751 zones and no zone) got the same prior probability,
$P(\text{no zone})$ would be only $1/752$, just because there are many ways to place a
zone. The prior for the zero case should instead reflect how likely we think it is
that a zone exists. We set $P(\text{no zone})=1/2$ and spread the rest uniformly over $\mathcal G$:
$$
P(\text{no zone})=\tfrac12,\qquad p(T,B)=\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac{1}{|\mathcal G|},\ (T,B)\in\mathcal G ,
$$
$$
P(\text{no zone}\mid\vd)=\frac{\tfrac12\,p(\vd\mid\text{no zone})}
{\tfrac12\,p(\vd\mid\text{no zone})+\tfrac12\,\frac1{|\mathcal G|}\sum_{\mathcal G}p(\vd\mid T,B)} .
$$

```{r p2b}
# ---- 2b ----
p0 <- 1 / 2
prob_nozone <- function(z, d) {
  l0 <- log(p0) + loglik(d, zone_mean(NA, NA))
  l1 <- log(1 - p0) + logsumexp(z$ll) - log(nrow(pairs))
  exp(l0 - logsumexp(c(l0, l1)))
}
p_nozone <- c(seis01 = prob_nozone(zone01, d01), seis02 = prob_nozone(zone02, d02))
```

This gives $P(\text{no zone}\mid\vd)=`r signif(p_nozone[1], 2)`$ for seis01 and $`r signif(p_nozone[2], 2)`$ for seis02.

## 2c)

Let $a_1$ = invest and $a_0$ = do not invest, with loss equal to minus the profit:
$$
L(a_1,V)=-(aV-b),\qquad L(a_0,V)=0 .
$$
The Bayes decision minimises the expected posterior loss. Since
$E\{L(a_1,V)\mid\vd\}=-(aE(V\mid\vd)-b)$ and $E\{L(a_0,V)\mid\vd\}=0$, the rule is
$$
\text{invest}\iff E(V\mid\vd)>\frac ba = 10 .
$$
We find $E(V\mid\vd)$ by simulation: draw $(T,B)$ (or no zone) from the posterior in 2b,
draw $\vm$ from the posterior in 1a with prior mean $\mu_m^{T,B}$, and compute $V$.

```{r p2c}
# ---- 2c ----
a <- 1; b <- 10; nsim <- 5000
K <- S_prior %*% t(A) %*% solve(S_d)
L_post <- t(chol(post00$cov + 1e-10 * diag(n)))

sim_volume <- function(z, d, p_no) {
  w <- c(p_no, (1 - p_no) * z$prob)
  Ts <- c(NA, pairs$T); Bs <- c(NA, pairs$B)
  pick <- sample(length(w), nsim, replace = TRUE, prob = w)
  sapply(pick, function(k) {
    mu_k <- zone_mean(Ts[k], Bs[k])
    m <- mu_k + K %*% (d - A %*% mu_k) + L_post %*% rnorm(n)
    volume(m)
  })
}
set.seed(5)
V01 <- sim_volume(zone01, d01, p_nozone[1])
V02 <- sim_volume(zone02, d02, p_nozone[2])
profit <- list(seis01 = a * V01 - b, seis02 = a * V02 - b)

profit_tab <- t(sapply(profit, function(x)
  c(mean(x + b) / a, mean(x), mean(x < 0), quantile(x, c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9)))))
knitr::kable(profit_tab, digits = 2,
             col.names = c("E(V|d)", "E(profit|d)", "P(profit<0|d)", "P10", "P50", "P90"),
             caption = "Posterior summaries of $V$ and the profit $aV-b$ (5000 simulations).")
```

```{r profithist, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=3, fig.cap="Posterior distribution of the profit $V-10$. Red line: break-even."}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
for (nm in names(profit)) {
  hist(profit[[nm]], breaks = 30, col = "grey80", border = "white", main = nm,
       xlab = "Profit", xlim = range(-5, profit[[nm]]))
  abline(v = 0, col = "red", lwd = 2)
}
```

We recommend investing in both cases, since $E(V\mid\vd)$ is far above 10 and none of
the 5000 simulations gave a loss. The uncertainty is shown by the profit histograms
and the percentiles in the table.

# Part 3

## 3a)

We write $\vm=\mu1-\Delta\mu\,1_{[T,B]}+x$ with $x\sim N(0,\Sigma_m)$
independent of $\mu\sim N(\mu_0,\tau_\mu^2)$. By double expectation and total variance,
\begin{align*}
E(\vm) &= E\{E(\vm\mid\mu)\}=\mu_01-\Delta\mu\,1_{[T,B]},\\
\operatorname{Cov}(\vm) &= E\{\operatorname{Cov}(\vm\mid\mu)\}+\operatorname{Cov}\{E(\vm\mid\mu)\}
=\Sigma_m+\tau_\mu^211^\top ,
\end{align*}
and therefore
$$
E(\vd)=\vA E(\vm),\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}(\vd)=\vA\Sigma_m\vA^\top+\tau_\mu^2(\vA 1)(\vA 1)^\top+\sigma_\varepsilon^2\vI .
$$
With $\mu_0=0$ the mean is unchanged. The rows of $\vA$ sum to zero, so
$\vA 1=0$ and the extra term disappears. So $p(\vd\mid T,B)$ and
$p(T,B\mid\vd)$ are the same as in 2a.

```{r p3a}
# ---- 3a ----
tau2 <- 0.25
S_prior_mu <- S_prior + tau2 * matrix(1, n, n)
S_d_mu <- A %*% S_prior_mu %*% t(A) + s2e * diag(n)
zone01_mu <- post_TB(d01, L = t(chol(S_d_mu)))
max_diff <- max(abs(zone01_mu$prob - zone01$prob))
```

Recomputing for seis01 gives the same posterior (largest difference
`r signif(max_diff, 2)`). This is not surprising, since the data say nothing about
the overall level of $\vm$.

## 3b)

With $\sigma_\varepsilon^2=\nu\sigma_m^2$ and $R=\Sigma_m/\sigma_m^2$ (the correlation
matrix), $\operatorname{Cov}(\vd)=\sigma_m^2C$ with $C=\vA R\vA^\top+\nu\vI$, so
for a given $(T,B)$
$$
p(\vd\mid\sigma_m^2,T,B)\propto(\sigma_m^2)^{-n/2}\exp\Big\{-\frac{Q_{T,B}}{2\sigma_m^2}\Big\},\qquad
Q_{T,B}=(\vd-\vA\mu_m^{T,B})^\top C^{-1}(\vd-\vA\mu_m^{T,B}).
$$
The conjugate prior is $\sigma_m^2\sim\mathrm{IG}(\alpha,\beta)$, and then
$$
p(\sigma_m^2\mid\vd,T,B)\propto(\sigma_m^2)^{-(\alpha+n/2)-1}\exp\Big\{-\frac{\beta+Q_{T,B}/2}{\sigma_m^2}\Big\}
\;\Rightarrow\;
\sigma_m^2\mid\vd,T,B\sim\mathrm{IG}\big(\alpha+\tfrac n2,\ \beta+\tfrac12Q_{T,B}\big).
$$
Since $(T,B)$ is unknown,
$p(\sigma_m^2\mid\vd)=\sum_{\mathcal G}p(T,B\mid\vd)\,\mathrm{IG}(\sigma_m^2;\alpha+\frac n2,\beta+\frac12Q_{T,B})$,
with $p(T,B\mid\vd)$ from 3c. We use $\alpha=2$, $\beta=1$ (prior mean 1) and $\nu=0.04$.

```{r p3b}
# ---- 3b ----
alpha <- 2; beta <- 1; nu <- 0.04
C <- A %*% (S_prior / s2m) %*% t(A) + nu * diag(n)
L_C <- t(chol(C))
quad_form <- function(d) sapply(1:nrow(pairs), function(k) {
  e <- forwardsolve(L_C, d - A %*% zone_mean(pairs$T[k], pairs$B[k]))
  sum(e^2)
})

# p(T, B | d) with s2m integrated out (used in 3c)
post_TB_t <- function(Q) {
  lw <- -(alpha + n / 2) * log(beta + Q / 2)
  exp(lw - logsumexp(lw))
}
Q01 <- quad_form(d01); Q02 <- quad_form(d02)
zone01_t <- post_TB_t(Q01); zone02_t <- post_TB_t(Q02)

# draws from p(s2m | d), a mixture of inverse gammas
draw_s2m <- function(Q, w, k = 20000) {
  j <- sample(length(w), k, replace = TRUE, prob = w)
  1 / rgamma(k, shape = alpha + n / 2, rate = beta + Q[j] / 2)
}
set.seed(6)
s2m_01 <- draw_s2m(Q01, zone01_t); s2m_02 <- draw_s2m(Q02, zone02_t)
s2m_tab <- rbind(seis01 = c(mean(s2m_01), quantile(s2m_01, c(0.025, 0.975))),
                 seis02 = c(mean(s2m_02), quantile(s2m_02, c(0.025, 0.975))))
knitr::kable(s2m_tab, digits = 2, col.names = c("posterior mean", "2.5%", "97.5%"),
             caption = "Posterior mean and 95\\% credibility interval for $\\sigma_m^2$.")
```

```{r p3bplot, fig.width=6, fig.height=3.2, fig.cap="Prior IG(2,1) (grey) and posterior densities of $\\sigma_m^2$ for seis01 and seis02."}
dinvgamma <- function(x, a, b) exp(a * log(b) - lgamma(a) - (a + 1) * log(x) - b / x)
dens_s2m <- function(x, Q, w) sapply(x, function(v) sum(w * dinvgamma(v, alpha + n / 2, beta + Q / 2)))

x <- seq(0.05, 2.5, length.out = 400)
f01 <- dens_s2m(x, Q01, zone01_t)
f02 <- dens_s2m(x, Q02, zone02_t)
plot(x, f01, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "darkgreen", ylim = c(0, max(f01, f02)),
     xlab = expression(sigma[m]^2), ylab = "Density")
lines(x, f02, lwd = 2, col = "darkorange")
lines(x, dinvgamma(x, alpha, beta), lwd = 2, col = "grey60")
legend("topright", c("prior", "seis01", "seis02"), lwd = 2,
       col = c("grey60", "darkgreen", "darkorange"), bty = "n")
```

## 3c)

We account for the uncertainty by integrating $\sigma_m^2$ out:
$$
p(\vd\mid T,B)=\int p(\vd\mid\sigma_m^2,T,B)\,p(\sigma_m^2)\,d\sigma_m^2
\;\propto\;\Big(\beta+\tfrac12Q_{T,B}\Big)^{-(\alpha+n/2)}
$$
(a multivariate Student-$t$ density), so
$p(T,B\mid\vd)\propto(\beta+\frac12Q_{T,B})^{-(\alpha+n/2)}$, compared with
$\propto\exp(-\frac12Q_{T,B})$ for fixed $\sigma_m^2=1$.

```{r p3c}
# ---- 3c ----
compare <- function(p_fix, p_t) {
  i <- which.max(p_fix); j <- which.max(p_t)
  c(mode_fix = paste0("(", pairs$T[i], ",", pairs$B[i], ")"), prob_fix = round(p_fix[i], 3),
    dZ_fix = round(sum(p_fix * pairs$dZ), 2),
    mode_t = paste0("(", pairs$T[j], ",", pairs$B[j], ")"), prob_t = round(p_t[j], 3),
    dZ_t = round(sum(p_t * pairs$dZ), 2))
}
cmp_tab <- rbind(seis01 = compare(zone01$prob, zone01_t), seis02 = compare(zone02$prob, zone02_t))
knitr::kable(cmp_tab, col.names = c("mode", "prob.", "E(dZ|d)", "mode", "prob.", "E(dZ|d)"),
             caption = "Posterior of $(T,B)$ with fixed $\\sigma_m^2=1$ (columns 1--3) and with $\\sigma_m^2$ integrated out (columns 4--6).")
```

The most likely pair is the same, but the posterior is slightly wider: the
probability of the mode drops from `r cmp_tab[1, "prob_fix"]` to `r cmp_tab[1, "prob_t"]`
(seis01) and from `r cmp_tab[2, "prob_fix"]` to `r cmp_tab[2, "prob_t"]` (seis02).
